- (c) Rekor is pinned to v1 by .github/policy/cosign-signing-config.json (cosign v3.1.3 `--signing-config`, an advisor-visible change to the pinned cosign command line: the default would use the TUF signing config, which may name Rekor v2 with no signed entry timestamp), and the log key in the trust file is the v1 key only; the identity is read from that one DER and openssl verifies a PEM re-made from the same DER (before this, text or base64 before a genuine block was skipped by openssl but read as the identity by the homemade DER reader, so a self-made certificate with the right identity placed before any genuine certificate was accepted); every JSON reader is UTF-8 only (UTF-16/32 are refused, not guessed). - `sign --check` and `check-build-record` take exactly one of --template (the committed template: the per-tag policy is made there from GITHUB_REF) and --policy (a finished policy); it names the file of Rekor entries a bundle carries. - Opus N-9 is left as a documented note (no change). - Step-8 round 3 (B-1, both seats): the time of a timestamp is read ONLY from the bare token that the timestamp authority signed (a whole response is first required to have a clean status, no status string other than the TSA default ("unspecified") and no failure info, and is then reduced to its token with `openssl ts -reply -token_out`; the TSA's signature is verified over that same token), because a response's status section lies outside the TSA's signature and an edited statusString `x\nTime stamp: <date>` used to set the time compared with the certificate's validity; the stamp form is bound to the record type (a Witness collection carries the bare token `tsp`, the provenance the whole response `rfc3161-response`; the signed release policy either, PR 4 decides) and a mismatch is refused; a genTime with milliseconds is read and the fraction dropped; a certificate with a repeated extension (a second SAN, a second Build Config URI) is refused; the DER reader is not a general parser and trusts only the structure of a Fulcio-signed certificate. - `actions` follows a listed local composite action wherever it is stored, including under .github/workflows/, and skips following only a reference that names a .yml/.yaml file (a reusable workflow, judged as a workflow of its own). - The token of the key and token attempts must name exactly <repo>/.github/workflows/stage-sign.yml@<ref> of this repository (GITHUB_REPOSITORY). - Codex security round 1 (Oct 10): - (S1) after cosign, `sign` refuses a bundle with no or an empty timestamp list or Rekor entry list, naming each, verifies the two files it wrote as stage sign and requires the payload cosign signed to be, as parsed JSON with exact types (true is not 1, 1 is not 1.0), the statement Sign built (Opus round-1 verify F1, H2) before it prints ok; genTime keeps its fraction (12:00:00.5 is after a certificate ending 12:00:00; for the certificate window openssl's check at the whole second below already decides, the fraction decides the 10-minute allowance after the verification clock, and a case pins that); a Rekor entry's logIndex and integratedTime must be canonical decimal strings, which fits the protobuf-JSON Sigstore bundle (int64 as strings): the Rekor REST API writes these fields as JSON numbers, which are refused, so the later pull request that produces the --rekor-stub file must take the entries from the bundle or emit protobuf-JSON strings; docs/quality/traceability.md|> No new required check: auditor-review-gate is not required per pull request on main (the owner took it off the ruleset on Nov 12 2026; release-only-checks.json still has release admission require it), so a missing record blocks the box merger's clearance, not GitHub's merge button. It therefore lands only after the writer (a later pull request) and the dispatch that calls it exist, on the landing day, together with the ruleset rule that only the writer creates branches under audit/** (the release manager's step). The record commit adds one file, audit-record, because the API can only make a commit that changes something. The Dependabot rule (AC9 to AC12) changes only the judge and the record writer. The gate workflow, its check name and the required checks are unchanged. Without a passing record, a Dependabot head passes only on the reviewer's success on that head, or, with no verdict of its own, as a clean merge of main into a head that passes this way.

docs/quality/traceability.md|> AC14 design decision (automated review round 1, B2): a non-plain version of a table tool is a HIT only on the records the databases return for it. A version with no OSV record and no GitHub advisory (cosign@latest, or the (default) pins of cosign and kind in the real tree) reads clean, deliberately: with no record nothing is known to be affected at any version, and making every non-plain pin a hit would open a daily issue forever with nothing to report. The rule is about the verdict on records, not about the pin. AC14 evaluation: range events are evaluated as OSV evaluates them: sorted by version (introduced 0 is the minimum, at one version the fixed wins), last_affected inclusive; Go versions compare as strict semver (pseudo-versions, numeric pre-releases and +incompatible are valid; r1, p1, post1 and rev1 are pre-release identifiers). A limit event is refused in SEMVER and ECOSYSTEM ranges (the record is a hit, a fail-closed refusal): the Go vulnerability database never writes limit, the OSV schema text could not be consulted offline, so any use of it in a Go range is treated as unreadable, which also removes the any-or-all question for several limits (the evaluator, used for other ecosystems, reads below ANY limit as affected). The schema asks for id and modified on a record, ecosystem and name on a package, an introduced event in every range (their order is free), and not both fixed and last_affected in one range; aliases may be absent or null. An independent interval oracle in the test compares the evaluator on a generated grid. The 240 recorded verdicts did not change. AC14 residual: the rule judges the OSV record's affected entries only; GitHub's ranges are read as before. An OSV answer that is not a record (not an object, no string id or modified) is a hit under the id UNREADABLE-OSV-RECORD; a GIT range together with a SEMVER or ECOSYSTEM range in one entry is a hit in every branch. The gh and git calls of pin-audit.py and of the shared helpers in pin-age-check.py have a 120 s timeout that stops the run (exit 2). AC14 residual (semver): bounds that SemVer 2.0.0 forbids (a numeric pre-release identifier with a leading zero such as 3.0.0-01, an empty identifier in the pre-release or the build metadata) are unparsable and read as affected, so the record is a hit. Go pseudo-versions with a zero-time stamp (0.0.0-00010101000000-000000000000) are one valid alphanumeric identifier, because it contains a hyphen, and parse normally. Removed Nov 11 2026 with the wait for new versions: AC1 (Dependabot cooldown), AC3 (age measurement) and AC6 (re-run of the pull requests the wait stopped); their ids are not reused and the gaps are deliberate, like AC16/AC17 below. AC31 is also left empty here: it is held for the go.dev archive signature check, which a second pull request adds (the owner's rule 3 of Nov 11 2026); no AC31 exists until then. AC16/AC17 history: the AC16 and AC17 first accepted for this requirement (a lexer telling text from commands, pull request 272, closed: an open-ended class) are WITHDRAWN; the AC16 above replaces both, and there is no AC17 (the gap is deliberate). AC18 (literal downloads in install-build-tools.sh) belongs to pull request 271. AC16 design: the scan stays strict. A row is {file, form, key, line, ruling} plus an optional count (default 1): key is the scan's own 64-hex sha256 prefix (for a download, of the one command segment that names curl or wget), and line is the 64-hex sha256 prefix of the WHOLE whitespace-flattened line that segment sits in (the automated reviewer, pull request 273 round 1: a segment hash alone ruled the same segment inside another line that pipes it to sh); an item is ruled only when every occurrence in the head sits in a line a row names, and a row covers at most count occurrences of that line, so a second copy of a ruled line fails unless the row counts it. Editing the line other than in spaces and tabs (which the scan normalises) voids the row; changing only a row's ruling prose does not void it (the prose is the reason, not the identity). An occurrence is ADDED when the head has more of its (file, form, key, whole line) than the base (the automated reviewer, pull request 273 round 2: counting by key alone let an edit that kept the download segment, such as a ruled echo rewritten to pipe into sh, pass as no addition); a replay of the 150 first-parent commits of main from 7c6077b (Sep 11) to 09b30af (Oct 10) found no commit that this newly fails. A row never matches a line holding whitespace other than a space or a tab, or a line joined from a backslash-newline continuation: bash reads those differently from the flattening (automated review round 1); count is at most 100. Intended: editing only a row's ruling prose does not void it, and a space- or tab-only edit of the line stays ruled. The exceptions file must be strict JSON: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity (which Python's reader accepts) and a repeated key stop the check (exit 2). AC16 delta accepted by the reviewer Oct 10 (automated review round 3, P7): the given names the command hash (key) and the whole-line hash (line); the then states the count limit and the edited-line, whitespace and continuation failures. Limit of line identity (automated review round 3, P4; the maintainers' decision, Oct 10): shell CONTEXT is not part of a line's identity, so moving a line out of a heredoc (above its opener) or commenting the opener out keeps (file, form, key, line) and is no addition. Therefore a row is only ever written for a line that is HARMLESS IN ANY CONTEXT: read as a shell command it runs no download (a comment, an echo or printf, a cat into a file, Python source or a package list that bash cannot parse), and the reviewer reviews each row for exactly that; a row for a line that would download when run is the reviewer's to refuse. The test holds the text of each committed row's line and checks it is harmless that way. Allowed row forms (reviewer, Oct 10; the reviewer refuses any other row): (1) TEXT lines: a comment, a quoted or echoed string, a data heredoc (a stub body or its opener), Python or package-name text that bash cannot parse; (2) HARNESS ASSERTION lines, whose whole grammar is the single data structure HARNESS_WHITELIST in harness_form.py (written by the pin-age check's own test suite); anything it does not name is refused. In short: t "RULE" "TITLE" bash -c 'BODY' _ followed by at most nine path arguments "$NAME" or "$NAME/path" with NAME in work, CALLS; no expansion of any kind in RULE or TITLE (no $, backtick, backslash or quote); the body SINGLE-QUOTED (the automated reviewer, pull request 289: a double-quoted body let the outer shell splice a variable's value into the code) and naming the paths only as whole "$1".."$9"; the commands grep, test, [, cat and exit with one digit; grep in the shape grep OPTION... -- PATTERN ["$N"...]: the options -E, -q, -v and -Eq as bare words, -- REQUIRED before the pattern, the pattern a double-quoted word that does not start with - (or the bare '.'), file operands only "$N" (the automated reviewer, pull request 289 round 3: a double-quoted word in an option position is an option to grep); cat only as cat -- "$N"; test and [ only the file tests -f -s -e -d -r on a positional "$N" (never a literal path or a substitution: the automated reviewer, pull request 289 round 6), = and !=, and count comparisons between digits and "$(grep -c ...)" (never -v, -R or an arithmetic operand that is a name or expression: bash 5 evaluates $(...) there); the substitutions "$(grep -c OPTION... -- PATTERN "$N")" and "$(cat -- "$N")" only; no unquoted glob, brace, subscript or expansion word; and no character outside printable ASCII and tab (the automated reviewer, pull request 289). The test proves the whitelist closed: a complement enumeration of every token class outside it in every position (none accepted, none refused for another reason), and a mutation run that widens it by one token at a time and requires an unexpected acceptance or a refusal for another reason (reported apart). The role rules that live in the parser's code (a file test on a positional, cat with exactly one operand, a positional within the arguments) are pinned by code mutants that loosen each one and must be caught. A harness line that reads a test stub's call log matches whole ROLE-TAGGED fields of a log the stub writes from its own parse (opt, val, out, url, unk; brackets inside a word become _), never substrings of flattened text (the automated reviewer, pull request 289 round 4); the later rows pull request runs each such line against logs with the right words in the wrong roles, forged fields inside URLs and -o values imitating flags. Scope (maintainers, Oct 11): this pull request carries the FORM (the parser, HARNESS_WHITELIST pinned by its golden canonical sha256, the complement enumeration, the mutation run, the runtime corpus with synthetic lines in the shapes of the input refresh assertions) and the three comment rows; the rows for the input refresh harness lines, with the test of what each line asserts, come with those lines in a later rows pull request. HARNESS_WHITELIST is pinned by HARNESS_WHITELIST_GOLDEN in the test: any change to the grammar needs that value edited in the same reviewed diff. The test decides form (2) with a quote-aware parser (harness_form.py in the test) and proves each refused variant as its own case. The rows are read from the exceptions file beside the checkout the script runs from (in CI trusted/, the base branch), never from the pull request's tree; a missing default file is no rows; a malformed list (not a list, a row that is not an object, a missing, empty or extra field, a key or line that is not 16 lowercase hex, a JSON object that repeats a key, a count that is not a whole number from 1 to 100, a repeated row) stops the check with exit 2. AC15 limit: the pins nested inside an action are not counted as held, so a ruling for a pin that is only nested can be dormant, never dead. AC15 expectation (Oct 9): the three cosign rulings (GO-2024-2718, GO-2024-2719, GO-2023-2181) are ALIVE now because main pinned cosign 3.1.3 inside the 90-day history window (until commit 8a7512d); they become dormant (or dead, if a cosign 3.1.3 pin has appeared and they decide nothing) about 2026-12-14, 90 days after that pin left main, unless a cosign 3.1.3 pin is held again (pull request 249). Finding (Oct 9): with the corrected table paths, the existing package-name filter of the audit already clears cosign 3.1.3 against GO-2026-4309. The real work of AC14 is (1) the corrected table (goreleaser, osv and golangci-lint need their /v2 path), (2) GitHub names matched under both the bare and the /vMAJOR path so the five existing rulings keep working, (3) the log of ignored entries, (4) the OSV query by the /vMAJOR path.
